newsitem.title: USA: Oshman's sees long-term margin improvement.
newsitem.headline: Oshman's sees long-term margin improvement.

text.p: Oshman's Sporting Goods Inc said it expects short-term continued pressure on same store sales, but long term it sees imporved gross margins and store profitability.
In the first quarter, ended May 3, sales increased 6.9 percent to $88.4 million as sales from continuing stores increased 12.0 percent to $69.3 million, the company said.

It said the increase was attributable to sales contributions of $11.0 million from eight new megastores opened since the beginning of fiscal 1996 offset by a same store sales decrease of $3.6 million, or 5.8 percent.

Management attributes the decline in same store sales to several factors including, the impact of the company's liquidation sales in closing stores, lower inventory levels, reduced advertising expenditures and to some extent, increased competitive pressures, the company said.

Net earnings, which included a pretax gain on disposition of a leasehold interest of $1.9 million, were $541,000, or $0.09 per share, compared with a net loss of $1.2 million, or $0.21 per share, in the year ago quarter.
As previously announced, Oshman's intends to close 53 of its 84 traditional stores in the current fiscal year.
At the end of the first quarter, 20 of these stores had been closed and an additional 11 were closed by the end of May, the company said.

Net sales from discontinued stores, stores closed or targeted to close decreased $1.7 million in the first quarter compared with the year ago quarter, Oshman's said. During the latest quarter, comparable sales from discontinued stores, some of which were in liquidation, increased $5.3 million over the same period in the prior year, offset by the elimination of $7.0 million of sales from stores closed.

Chief Executive Alvin N. Lubetkin stated, "We are currently operating with approximately 15 percent less inventory per megastore than last year, and advertising and store payroll expenditures have been reduced.
"Short term, we expect some downward pressure on same store sales; however, longer term, we anticipate improved gross margins and store profitability."

The company opened one new SuperSports USA megastore in the first quarter of fiscal 1997 and intends to open an five more megastores this year. Oshman's operates 85 sporting goods' stores, including 32 megastores, located primarily in medium to large metropolitan areas across the United States.
